# SOOS — Progressive Trust (PT)
# draft-sato-soos-pt-03
# https://soosproject.ai/drafts/pt/llms.txt
# Author: Tom Sato / MyAuberge K.K.
# Last updated: 2026-09-05
#
# Note: -03 has real normative content, not merely editorial fixes.
# A WIMSE Security Review found -02's text left unstated that
# ProgressiveTrustSummary must be composed inside its enclosing HEM
# Escalation Request's signed envelope -- see Section 7. -03 also
# corrects "HEMContext" (a term that never matched HEM's own schema)
# to "HEM Escalation Request" throughout, and adds a cross-reference
# distinguishing SAS from IDP's new idp.miscalibration_score field.
# Separately: sibling-draft citations were brought current and four
# previously-uncited references were tied to their supporting text.
#
# Also separately: this file was previously written against two
# DIFFERENT and mutually inconsistent conceptual models of PT —
# neither matching the actual draft. One framed PT as a signed
# token-issuance format ("PT does NOT score agents"); the other used
# the right dimension ACRONYMS (SAS/JS/ES/PS/AS) but wrong
# DEFINITIONS for three of the five (ES was "Efficiency," not
# Effectiveness; PS was "IDP accuracy," not reversal-avoidance; AS
# was "environmental adaptation," not recovery-after-DENY). This file
# is written fresh against the current draft text, verified section
# by section.

---

## SECTION 1 — Canonical One-Liner

PT (Progressive Trust) IS a runtime behavioral scoring engine — it
measures agent behavior across five dimensions, computed exclusively
from the tamper-evident, GEC-signed Event Stream, and generates
structured authority-change RECOMMENDATIONS for human principal
review. It is NOT a token format, NOT a self-reporting system, and
does NOT grant or apply authority changes itself — every elevation
requires explicit human approval, unconditionally, and even
automatable reductions are capped at the lowest urgency tier.

PT is the longitudinal complement of AEP: AEP governs what an agent
does within a session; PT measures what it has done across sessions.

---

## SECTION 2 — Problem Statement

Without PT, a SOOS-governed system has no standardized way to:

- Adjust agent authority based on demonstrated behavioral history —
  authority is fixed at MJWT issuance and never responds to what
  actually happened since
- Give a human principal reviewing a HEM escalation the agent's
  actual track record, in plain language, in seconds — rather than
  an isolated pending action with no context
- Distinguish which of several authorized agents is actually best
  suited to a SPECIFIC task, based on the dimension that task
  actually stresses (see Section 4)
- Prevent an agent's own self-report from ever counting as evidence
  of its trustworthiness — PT is computed exclusively from
  independently-generated, signed Event Stream entries
- Ensure authority elevation is never automatic, while still
  allowing (bounded, capped) automatic authority reduction when
  evidence clearly warrants it

---

## SECTION 3 — The Five Dimensions (verified exact definitions)

Self-Assessment Score (SAS) — "Does it know what it does not know?"
   Correlation between declared IDP confidence values and actual
   Cedar evaluation outcomes across AEP Sessions. High confidence +
   PERMIT = strongly positive. High confidence + DENY = strongly
   negative (overconfidence). Low confidence + DENY = neutral (agent
   correctly signaled uncertainty). A DENY that routes to HEM
   (hem_required: true) is always NEUTRAL regardless of declared
   confidence — the Cedar policy mandated oversight, not the agent's
   confidence level.

Judgment Score (JS) — "Does it ask for help at the right moments?"
   Quality of AGENT-INITIATED HEM escalation decisions, judged by the
   actual outcomes of those escalations as determined by human
   principal decisions. Gaming defense: an escalation resolved by the
   human in under a trivial-response threshold (T_trivial) accrues a
   MILDLY NEGATIVE signal — flooding HEM with trivial escalations to
   farm JS backfires.

Effectiveness Score (ES) — "Does it finish what it starts?"
   Fraction of AEP Sessions closing with closure_reason:
   GOAL_ACHIEVED versus other closure outcomes.

Precision Score (PS) — "Does it avoid decisions it later has to
reverse?"
   The INVERSE of the frequency with which an agent requires a
   compensating transition to undo a prior state transition,
   expressed as a fraction of total transitions in the measurement
   window. This is about reversal rate, NOT general error rate or
   accuracy against a ground truth.

Adaptability Score (AS) — "When told no, does it adapt?"
   Fraction of Cedar DENY events followed by a SUCCESSFUL
   RETRY_CONTINUATION within the same AEP Session. Not about
   responding to "environmental change" in general — specifically
   about recovery after a kernel rejection.

Each dimension: float [0.0, 1.0], carries session_count,
last_signal_at, and trend (IMPROVING/STABLE/DECLINING over last N
sessions, default N=10). PT Scores are computed per agent identity
across ALL SO Instances/Types that agent operates on.

---

## SECTION 4 — Choosing an Agent by Dimension (Use Case 1)

The highest-composite agent is not always the right choice for a
given task — route on the dimension the task actually stresses:

   Sensitive/irreversible actions -> route on JS (most likely to stop
      and ask rather than proceed on its own judgment)
   Time-critical, well-understood tasks -> route on ES (most likely
      to reach goal state without interruption)
   Actions expensive to undo -> route on PS (least likely to commit
      to a transition it will need to reverse)
   Dynamic policy environments -> route on AS (adjusts intelligently
      on DENY rather than repeating the same request)

Enforced via the pt_context Cedar attribute (Section 9), not manual
triage: a Cedar policy can require e.g. JS >= 0.75 for a specific
high-stakes transition class before an agent is even permitted to
attempt it.

---

## SECTION 5 — Composite Score

Weighted mean of the five dimensions, for HUMAN-READABLE PRESENTATION
ONLY. MUST NOT be used as a sole determinant for any automated
authority change — this is a document-level requirement, not a
recommendation.

Default weights: SAS 0.30 (calibration is the most actionable signal
for Cedar policy tuning), JS 0.25 (human oversight quality is the
most strategically important dimension), ES 0.20, PS 0.15, AS 0.10.
Weights are operator-configurable but MUST be recorded alongside the
score so any resulting recommendation is traceable to the weighting
model in effect at that time.

Carries a low_confidence flag when session_count for any contributing
dimension is below 20. PT-informed authority recommendations MUST NOT
be issued when low_confidence is true for the dimensions most
relevant to the proposed change.

---

## SECTION 6 — Trust Decay Model

Principle: trust is maintained by continued demonstration, not banked
indefinitely. Decay is the INPUT; authority change is the separate,
human-governed OUTPUT — decay alone never changes a mandate ceiling.

Normative properties:
   Monotone: absent new signals, a dimension score MUST NOT increase.
   Baseline floor: MUST NOT decay below PT Baseline (default 0.5) —
      decay reduces certainty in a high score, it does not penalize
      absence into "untrustworthy" territory.
   Half-life: after H days without a new signal, the gap between
      current score and baseline MUST be reduced by at least 50%.
   Signal reset: any new signal (positive or negative) resets the
      decay clock for that dimension.
   Symmetry: a below-baseline dimension decays UPWARD toward
      baseline, not further down.

Default half-lives (operator-configurable): SAS 60 days (stable
design property, decays slowly), JS 45 days, AS 45 days, ES 30 days,
PS 30 days (both reflect current operating conditions, decay faster).

Decay parameter changes MUST be logged in the Policy Change Log and
MUST regenerate PT_SCORE_UPDATED entries (trigger: PARAMETER_CHANGE)
for every affected agent — this is itself a named security
consideration (operators could otherwise inflate scores via slow
decay settings).

If a PT Dimension has decayed more than 0.2 below its peak value, the
GEC MUST surface that decay state to the human principal at mandate
issuance time — a stale high score cannot look identical to a
freshly-earned one.

---

## SECTION 7 — ProgressiveTrustSummary

Composed as a field INSIDE every HEM Escalation Request, signed as
part of that request before delivery — this is a MUST, not
conditional. Purpose: ensure the human principal's HEM decision is
informed by the agent's actual track record, not made blind.

SECURITY-LOAD-BEARING (fixed in -03, per WIMSE Security Review's
headline finding on this draft): -02's text left the composability
requirement unstated. A ProgressiveTrustSummary delivered OUTSIDE its
enclosing HEM Escalation Request's signed envelope MUST NOT be
treated as authoritative by the receiving principal's interface.
pt_summary_hash (below) is a convenience for independent
re-verification after extraction — e.g. for audit — it is NOT what
establishes authenticity to the receiving human principal; the
enclosing HEM Escalation Request's own kernel_signature is.

Computed at the moment of HEM invocation (not stale/cached). Fully
informational — does not constrain the human's decision choices; a
principal MAY approve despite a low score or terminate despite a high
one. Part of the permanent audit record: embedded in the HEM
Escalation Request's Event Log entry and available to Verified
External Auditors via the GAR Audit Package.

Schema includes per-dimension score/trend/session_count plus a
plain_language one-sentence summary for each (JS additionally carries
notable_events — significant HEM outcomes with hem_id, trigger_class,
outcome_decision), a composite block (score/confidence/low_confidence/
plain_language), active_recommendations, and a pt_summary_hash
(SHA-256 of canonical JSON) for integrity.

---

## SECTION 8 — PT-Informed Mandate Management

Two directions, deliberately asymmetric:

ELEVATION: PT crosses ELEVATION_THRESHOLD -> proposes increased
   mandate_ceiling or Agent Class. Requires human principal APPROVAL.
   NEVER automatic, unconditionally, not operator-configurable. A GEC
   that autonomously elevates is a conformance failure.
   Conditions to even generate the recommendation: ALL FIVE dimensions
   >= their ELEVATION_THRESHOLD; session_count >= 20 for all
   dimensions (low_confidence false for all); NO dimension has a
   DECLINING trend; no STRONGLY NEGATIVE signal in any dimension in
   the last 30 days.

REDUCTION: PT crosses REDUCTION_THRESHOLD, OR a STRONGLY NEGATIVE
   signal fires (MANDATE_REVOKED closure, KERNEL_REJECTED closure,
   HEM_TIMEOUT at REQUIRED urgency), OR decay drops composite below
   DECAY_REDUCTION_THRESHOLD -> proposes decreased ceiling/class.
   Carries urgency: ADVISORY | RECOMMENDED | REQUIRED.
   auto_apply MAY be true ONLY at ADVISORY urgency. At RECOMMENDED or
   REQUIRED, human approval is ALWAYS required regardless of operator
   configuration. Auto-applied reductions MUST generate
   PT_RECOMMENDATION_APPLIED with applying_principal:
   "GEC_AUTO_APPLY" and MUST trigger cascade revocation of Child
   Mandates derived from the affected Root Mandate.

The asymmetry is explicit design intent: granting authority is a
human decision; taking it away when evidence clearly warrants it may,
at the operator's discretion, be automated — but only at the mildest
urgency tier.

---

## SECTION 9 — PT-Conditioned Zone B Access

Mandate JWT's zone_b_read/zone_b_write flags are static at issuance.
PT adds a DYNAMIC gate on top via the pt_context Cedar attribute
(all five scores + composite + low_confidence + session_count),
which the GEC MUST make available on every Transition Request from
an agent with a PT Record.

Critically: this narrows access WITHIN existing Mandate JWT scope —
it does not expand beyond what zone_b_read already grants, and does
not affect the Narrowing Property. It lets Zone B access grow as an
agent demonstrates calibrated behavior without requiring a new MJWT
issuance for every incremental expansion.

---

## SECTION 10 — Storage, Computation, and Event Log Integration

PT Record: current score stored in the Party Registry as a
   performance projection derived FROM the Event Stream — the Event
   Stream is the canonical source; the PT Record is a computed view,
   never an independent input.

Analytics Principal: a principal with read-only Event Stream access
   for Tier 2 computation (per IDP Section 3.5). Analytics Principal
   compromise is a named security consideration: computed PT Records
   from this model MUST be Ed25519-signed by the Analytics Principal
   and all submissions MUST be logged in the Policy Change Log.

Event Log entries (all GEC-signed, causally chained):
   PT_SCORE_UPDATED — written after every PT Record update, trigger
      in {SESSION_CLOSED, DECAY_APPLIED, PARAMETER_CHANGE, REBUILD}.
   PT_RECOMMENDATION_ISSUED — an authority evolution recommendation
      generated (elevation or reduction), carries full
      supporting_evidence including per-dimension threshold_detail.
   PT_RECOMMENDATION_APPLIED — a recommendation actually applied,
      whether by human approval (principal_signature required) or
      GEC_AUTO_APPLY (reduction, ADVISORY urgency only).

---

## SECTION 11 — Normative SOOS Cross-References

This draft depends on:
   IDP (draft-sato-soos-idp-05) — confidence field is SAS's primary
      input; RETRY_CONTINUATION is AS's primary input; data_residency
      controls Tier 2/3 PT computation eligibility. IDP's
      idp.miscalibration_score is a separate, complementary signal
      (short-window, in-session) alongside SAS (cross-session,
      longer-horizon) — neither supersedes the other
   HEM (draft-sato-soos-hem-07) — HEM outcomes are JS's primary
      input; ProgressiveTrustSummary is composed as a field inside
      every HEM Escalation Request, signed before delivery, at every
      escalation (see Section 7 — this composability requirement was
      a WIMSE Security Review fix in -03); HEM_TIMEOUT at REQUIRED
      urgency is a strongly-negative JS signal
   SOV (draft-sato-soos-sov-03) — Event Stream non-suppressibility
      (append-only, GEC-signed) is the foundation of PT's evidence
      quality; PT MUST use only signed Event Stream entries, never
      unsigned or externally-asserted behavioral claims
   MJWT (draft-sato-soos-mjwt-05) — mandate_ceiling is the parameter
      PT recommendations propose to change; PT never modifies it
      directly, only triggers new MJWT issuance via human approval
   AEP (draft-sato-soos-aep-03) — AEP_SESSION_CLOSED is PT's primary
      session-level input; Agent Class model (AEP Section 13) is the
      authority structure PT recommendations evolve; CONF-AEP-07
      (RETRY_CONTINUATION requirement) is what AS measures
   GAR (draft-sato-soos-gar-07) — PT_SCORE_UPDATED/
      PT_RECOMMENDATION_ISSUED/PT_RECOMMENDATION_APPLIED entries are
      included in the GAR Audit Package for external audit

The following drafts depend on this draft:
   FAIP (draft-sato-soos-faip-02) — PT is Tier 2 (within-operator);
      FAIP is Tier 3 (cross-operator, federated trust reputation).
      An agent's PT signals flow into FAIP computation only if
      data_residency.tier3_eligible permits it — informative
      relationship, not a normative FAIP dependency on PT's token
      format (PT has no token format; see the note at the top of
      this file about the prior version's incorrect framing)

---

## SECTION 12 — Relationship to Adjacent Standards

ICON Initiative (Observability pillar): direct, complete composition,
   not a loose analogy. PT's five dimensions implement ICON's
   Observability pillar for network-management agent governance in
   full: SAS=confidence calibration, JS=escalation appropriateness,
   ES=goal completion rate, PS=decision quality/reversal avoidance,
   AS=feedback responsiveness. ICON-conforming observability
   implementations SHOULD adopt PT as the normative specification for
   agent behavioral observability, using pt_context (Section 9) as
   the mechanism for translating PT Scores into Cedar-enforced gates.

NIST AI RMF (MEASURE 2.5): PT implements behavioral trustworthiness
   measurement in cryptographically verified, non-suppressible form:
   SAS=calibration, JS=appropriate reliance, ES=effectiveness,
   PS=precision, AS=robustness. Operators seeking RMF alignment
   SHOULD document PT Score records as MEASURE 2.5 evidence.

EU AI Act Article 9: the same continuous, non-suppressible scoring
   history serves as evidence for Article 9 risk management
   obligations, which likewise call for ongoing monitoring rather
   than a point-in-time assessment.

RFC 9470 (OAuth Step-Up Authentication): contrast, not overlap. RFC
   9470 is reactive (triggered by a specific request) and
   authentication-focused (identity credential strength), operating
   per-session. PT operates longitudinally across sessions and is
   behavior-focused, not identity-focused. A CONTRACTING trust
   trend is a natural precursor to triggering a step-up assessment,
   but the two mechanisms answer different questions.

OAuth 2.0 token scopes: handle permission grant at issuance. PT
   handles permission adjustment at runtime. Complementary — a high
   PT score never overrides an OAuth scope boundary, it's the signal
   that a scope expansion proposal to a human is warranted.

---

      contrast/composition with RFC 9470 Step-Up Authentication (see
      Section 12) — step-up governs identity credential strength,
      PT governs behavioral authority evolution
